findings.claim: The global shortcut handler calls event.preventDefault() before the editable-target and open-dialog guards, so Cmd/Ctrl+K is swallowed (browser/editor default blocked) inside inputs, textareas, selects, and contenteditable controls even though the palette does not open.
findings.evidence: openCommandPalette: `if ((event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey) && event.key.toLowerCase() === "k") { event.preventDefault(); if (!isEditableTarget(event.target) && !hasOpenDialog()) { setCommandPaletteOpen(true); } }` — preventDefault runs unconditionally on every matching keydown.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the guards before preventDefault: `if (isEditableTarget(event.target) || hasOpenDialog()) return; event.preventDefault(); setCommandPaletteOpen(true);`

findings.claim: hasOpenDialog() disables the global palette shortcut whenever ANY element with role="dialog" is mounted anywhere in the document — including non-modal or CSS-hidden dialogs — silently dead-keying Cmd/Ctrl+K app-wide.
findings.evidence: `function hasOpenDialog(): boolean { return document.querySelector('[role="dialog"]') !== null; }` — a DOM-global presence check with no visibility/modality filtering; any feature dialog (e.g., the chat ToolApprovalDialog present in the repo) or a permanently-mounted hidden dialog suppresses the shortcut.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the check to visible modal dialogs (e.g., query for `[role="dialog"][aria-modal="true"]` and verify offsetParent/getClientRects), or track open dialogs in the UI store instead of scraping the DOM.

findings.claim: The brand-parity test reads `../docs/ui/logo`, escaping the frontend package root; that directory is absent from the packet file tree (only `./docs/ui` is listed) and from any frontend-isolated context (frontend/Dockerfile, frontend CI boundary checks), so the test throws ENOENT or fails outside a full monorepo checkout.
findings.evidence: `const delivered = filesBelow(resolve(projectRoot, "../docs/ui/logo"))` where projectRoot is `frontend`; the diff adds no files under `docs/ui/logo/`, so the assertion depends on untracked-in-this-change state.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert against a manifest checked into the frontend package (e.g., an explicit expected-file list in the test), or copy the delivered inventory into `frontend/public/brand/` and compare against that.

findings.claim: The manifest now ships a single 512x512 icon with purpose "any", dropping the previous 180x180 "any maskable" entry; Chrome's PWA installability criteria expect both a ~192px-class and a 512px icon, and removing "maskable" causes adaptive-icon cropping on Android.
findings.evidence: Diff: `- "src": "/apple-touch-icon.png", "sizes": "180x180", "purpose": "any maskable"` replaced by `+ "src": "/brand/png/uar-appicon-dark-512.png", "sizes": "512x512", "purpose": "any"` — despite 128/256px PNGs being added in the same diff and left unreferenced.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 192 (or 256) entry alongside the 512, and mark at least one icon `"purpose": "maskable"` (or "any maskable").

findings.claim: The checked-in built bundle under `static/` (index.html, manifest.json, apple-touch-icon.png — present in the file tree, with `src/embedded.rs` suggesting it is embedded into the server binary) is not updated, so it still references the retired `/favicon.svg` and `/apple-touch-icon.png` and contains none of the new `/brand/*` assets; until a rebuild is committed, the served/embedded artifact 404s the new favicon/manifest paths or shows stale branding.
findings.evidence: File tree lists `./static/index.html`, `./static/apple-touch-icon.png`, `./static/manifest.json`, `./static/.vite`; the diff changes only `frontend/index.html` and `frontend/public/manifest.json` and adds brand assets only under `frontend/public/brand/`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either regenerate and commit `static/` in this change, or remove `static/` from version control and document that it is build output.

findings.claim: The spec's motion-accessibility requirement ('Interactive state transitions ... SHALL become effectively immediate under reduced-motion preference') is not implemented: every new shell transition uses plain `transition-*`/`duration-200` utilities with no `motion-reduce:` variant or reduced-motion CSS anywhere in the diff.
findings.evidence: specs/frontend-app-shell/spec.md Requirement 'Shell interactions preserve Flat 2.0 and motion accessibility' vs. `transition-[width] duration-200` (nav-rail), `transition-opacity duration-200`, `transition-[translate,opacity] duration-200` (command-palette, mobile-sheet-host), `transition-transform duration-200` (skip link in app-shell.tsx) — none carry `motion-reduce:` guards and no global reduced-motion rule is added in the diff.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:transform-none` to the transitioning shell elements, or add a global `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` rule zeroing transition duration.

findings.claim: runtime-settings claims the bare `/admin` path via exactMatchPaths, so the admin landing route's breadcrumb and Configure-tab state read 'Configure / Runtime settings' regardless of which default admin surface actually renders there.
findings.evidence: `exactMatchPaths: ["/admin"]` on the `runtime-settings` destination; BreadcrumbHeader derives section/label from findDestinationForPath, so `/admin` resolves to 'Runtime settings' even though the legacy shell treated `/admin` as a generic landing.
findings.suggested_fix: Point `/admin` at the destination that actually renders there, or add a redirect from `/admin` to a concrete destination and drop the exactMatchPaths entry.

findings.claim: Cmd/Ctrl+K cannot close the palette once open: the open palette itself satisfies hasOpenDialog() and its input satisfies isEditableTarget(), so the shortcut is a no-op — a regression from the removed admin-shell handler which toggled `setCommandOpen((open) => !open)`.
findings.evidence: Deleted admin-shell hunk: `setCommandOpen((open) => !open)` toggle; new handler only ever calls `setCommandPaletteOpen(true)` and both guards block re-entry while the palette dialog is mounted.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow the shortcut to toggle: if the command palette is the only open dialog, call `setCommandPaletteOpen(false)` instead of returning.
